q: What is the allowable maximum TGFA of a basic R-2 building without a firewall on an inside (regular) lot?
n: For basic R-2 without firewalls the inside or regular lot is the tightest column at 3 x 60% of the total lot area. The interior, corner, through and corner-through lots all take 3 x 70%.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII, Table VII.1 - allowable maximum TGFA

q: What is the allowable maximum TGFA of a basic R-2 building without a firewall on an interior (rear) or end lot?
n: Basic R-2 without firewalls takes 3 x 70% of the total lot area on an interior or end lot. Only the inside or regular lot drops to 3 x 60%.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII, Table VII.1 - allowable maximum TGFA

q: What is the allowable maximum TGFA of a basic R-2 building without a firewall on a through lot?
n: The through lot takes the same 3 x 70% as the interior, corner and corner-through lots. The number of storeys changes to 5 only for maximum R-2, not basic R-2.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII, Table VII.1 - allowable maximum TGFA

q: What is the allowable maximum TGFA of a maximum R-2 building without a firewall on an inside (regular) lot?
n: Maximum R-2 without firewalls raises the storey multiplier from 3 to 5 but keeps the same percentages, so the inside or regular lot is 5 x 60% and the other lot types are 5 x 70%.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII, Table VII.1 - allowable maximum TGFA

q: What is the allowable maximum TGFA of a basic R-2 building WITH a firewall on a corner lot?
n: Building with firewalls raises the percentages: basic R-2 with firewalls takes 3 x 75% on the corner lot and 3 x 70% only on the inside or regular lot.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Rule VII, Table VII.1 - allowable maximum TGFA

q: Which certificate does the Office of the Building Official issue when the electrical work of a building is finally completed?
n: NBC Form E-05 is the Certificate of Final Electrical Inspection. E-04 covers inspection during the work and E-06 the annual inspection of an occupied building.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), NBC Form E-05
